question: T12 (task-054ab7d89ad4da4b): on the desktop, Wave Intensity from 180 down to 0 one step at a time on a Scrolling block made taller by hand than its line needs: does each step take one row off (as the one-step fall in CAP-T12HANDFALL does), or does it end where one press 180 to 0 ends? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10). Then 'open' (select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design), a press on Wave Intensity at the range's end (180: 1/2/7/26), 'go' (Escape and a press on the page); 'place i r0/c0/r1/c1' moves and resizes block i by hand: the Scrolling block to 1/2/12/26 (11 rows, its line needs 6), the Text block to 1/14/3/20 (A plans, other columns) or 8/2/13/10 (B plans, CAP-T12HANDFALL L1's). Then 'open' and the plan's steps: A1 and B1 a drag one value at a time, pressed on 180 and moved to 150, 120, 90, 60, 30 and 0, 300 ms apart, read 80 ms after each move and 400 and 1200 ms after the last, let go there (one DevTools session, 'inputs'); A2 and B2 a press on the thumb at 180 (no change), then six real ArrowLeft keys 1.2 s apart, read 60 ms and 1.2 s after each in the keys' own DevTools session ('keys': states with the layout L and the range's state st); A3 six presses, 150 to 0; A4 one press on 0. Then 'go' and Cmd+Z until as built. R1 and R2 are two sessions each (R1a and R1b, R2a and R2b, probe-z.mjs), with plans of other tasks in the same sessions. Exit without saving each time.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, the range's value). The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: Each step takes one row, by a drag one value at a time (A1, B1), by ArrowLeft keys (A2, B2) and by presses (A3): from 1/2/12/26 at 180 the Scrolling block goes to 1/2/11/26 at 150, 1/2/10/26 at 120, 1/2/9/26, 1/2/8/26, 1/2/7/26 and 1/2/6/26 at 0 (5 rows for a 34 px line that needs 2). Each step is a one-step fall on a block that still has more rows than its line needed before it, so the CAP-T12HANDFALL rule holds at each one. The drag's rows are there 80 ms after each move, the keys' 60 ms after each key.

One press 180 to 0 (A4) takes it to 1/2/7/26 (6 rows): the height less the 180 px fall snapped to the row pitch (441 - 180 = 261 px), as CAP-T12WAVEDROP's falls of two steps or more. So steps one at a time end a row lower than one press.

With the Text block in other columns (A) the section's rows follow the Scrolling block's foot down, 12 to 6. With the Text block at 8/2/13/10 (B) it stays while it starts on or above the new foot (150 to 60, foot 11 to 8), then goes up by the foot's fall: 7/2/12/10 at 30 and 6/2/11/10 at 0; the section keeps the rows under it (12, 11, 10).

Undo: the drag is one undo step (one Cmd+Z gives back 1/2/12/26 and the Text block where it was); each key and each press is its own (six Cmd+Z go back one row each). R1 and R2 read alike in every read and every drag and key state (areas, rows, line, Undo and Redo, the range's value).
Not read: a block made taller by hand by other rows or in other columns, a drag with pauses of a second or more, other window widths, the phone view.
